grammar.title: Quantifiers: All, Both, Either, Neither, None, Few
grammar.explanation:
**Quantifiers** tell us how many or how much of something there is. **All**, **both**, **either**, **neither**, **none**, **most**, and **few** are common quantifiers.

Use **both**, **either**, and **neither** for two things. **Both** means the two together. **Either** means one or the other. **Neither** means not one and not the other.

Use **all**, **most**, and **none** for three or more. **All** means every one. **Most** means almost all. **None** means not one. For example, a large number of shoppers check the size before they buy. **None** of them wants the wrong size, and **most** of them read a review first.

Use **of** before the, my, these, and pronouns: **most of the** people, **all of them**, **both of us**. Without a determiner, do not use **of**: **most people**, not most of people.

**Each** and **every** take a singular noun and a singular verb. **Each student has** a book. **Every room has** a balcony.

**A few** means some, a small number, and it sounds positive. **Few** means not many, almost none, and it sounds negative. I have **a few** friends here, so I am happy. I have **few** friends here, so I am lonely.

Before a noun, use **no**, not none. There are **no** buses. **None** is used alone or with of: **None of** the buses came.
examples: * **Both** my brothers live in Canada. (two people)
* **Neither** of my parents speaks English. (not one and not the other)
*You can pay by card or in cash. **Either** is fine. (one or the other)
* **All** the shops close at 9 p.m. (three or more)
* **Most** people prefer summer to winter. (no of without the)
* **None** of the questions were easy. (none of + plural)
